::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}

:::{#sol-argmax-positive-multiple}

1. Completing the [square](algebra.qmd#def-square) gives

   $$
   \begin{aligned}
   g(x) &= 4x - x^2 \\
   &= 4 - (x - 2)^2.
   \end{aligned}
   $$

   The square $(x - 2)^2$ is never negative and is $0$ only at $x = 2$,
   so $g(x) \le 4 = g(2)$ for every $x \in [0, 4]$,
   with equality only at $x = 2$.
   So $\argmax_{x \in [0, 4]} g(x) = \cb{2}$.

2. Multiplying by $5$ gives

   $$
   \begin{aligned}
   f(x) &= 5\,g(x) \\
   &= 20 - 5\,(x - 2)^2.
   \end{aligned}
   $$

   By the same reasoning, $f(x) \le 20 = f(2)$ with equality only at $x = 2$,
   so $\argmax_{x \in [0, 4]} f(x) = \cb{2}$.
   This is the same [set](sets.qmd#def-set) as for $g$.
   The largest [value](functions.qmd#def-value) changes from $4$ to $20$,
   so the largest value is not the same.

:::

:::

::: {.content-visible when-format="revealjs"}
